title: The gym's web page lists personal training packs as membership fees, but the join page does not offer them
what: The gym's free web page builds its Fees board, its 'Plans from' price line, its Google price range and the facts its AI helper answers from out of every active plan, including personal training packs (which are add-ons sold on top of a gym plan). The join page right behind its Join button leaves those packs out. So a visitor can see a PT pack listed as a fee, or a 'Plans from' price that is a PT pack, then not find it when they tap Join. The web page also stops at 12 plans while the join page shows up to 40. The test gym has no PT packs, so this was read in the code, not seen.
expected: The web page and the join page show the same plans: ordinary gym plans only (or PT packs shown in their own add-on line), with the same limit.
who: people visiting a gym's web page, and gym owners who sell PT packs
how_often: every visit to the page of a gym that has an active PT pack
fix_line: Leave PT packs out of the web page's plan list as the join page does, and use the same plan limit

title: A person who paid online when joining shows as not paid on Today once the request is over 45 days old
what: Today's 'Joined online' card lists every open join request, however old. Whether each one was paid online comes from the payment server, which only returns join payments from the last 45 days (and at most 100). For a request left waiting longer than that, the paid payment is not returned, so the card shows 'pay at the desk' with Make member instead of Paid online and Approve, and the warning that stops a second charge cannot see the payment either. The desk can then take the fee again in cash. The test gym has no open join requests, so this was read in the code, not seen.
expected: The payment status on a join request is shown for as long as the request is open, however old it is.
who: desk staff and people who join online and pay
how_often: rare: only join requests left waiting more than 45 days
fix_line: Return join payments by the open requests' ids, not by a 45-day window
